extraction.name: Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD) v1.0
extraction.description: The Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD) is a new reading comprehension dataset consisting of 107,785 question-answer pairs on 536 Wikipedia articles, where the answer to each question is a segment of text from the corresponding reading passage. It is designed to be a challenging problem for future research in machine comprehension.
extraction.creator: Pranav Rajpurkar and Jian Zhang and Konstantin Lopyrev and Percy Liang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset collection was performed in three stages: curating passages, crowdsourcing question-answers on those passages, and obtaining additional answers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Over the development and test sets, 2.6% of questions were marked unanswerable by at least one of the additional crowdworkers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: High-quality articles were retrieved using Project Nayuki’s Wikipedia’s internal PageRanks to obtain the top 10000 articles of English Wikipedia, from which 536 articles were sampled uniformly at random.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: From each sampled Wikipedia article, individual paragraphs were extracted, stripping away images, figures, tables, and discarding paragraphs shorter than 500 characters. The articles were then partitioned randomly into a training set (80%), a development set (10%), and a test set (10%).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers were employed to create questions and answers. On each paragraph, workers were tasked with asking and answering up to 5 questions, entering questions in a text field and highlighting answers in the paragraph. Workers were guided by sample paragraphs and examples of good/bad questions/answers. They were encouraged to use their own words, with copy-paste functionality disabled on the paragraph text. For additional answers, crowdworkers were shown only questions and paragraphs, and asked to select the shortest span in the paragraph that answered the question. If unanswerable, they submitted the question without marking an answer.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Daemo platform (Gaikwad et al., 2015), with Amazon Mechanical Turk as its backend.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Human performance on the test set was 86.8% F1 based on inter-annotator agreement. Mismatch between human answers mostly occurred due to inclusion/exclusion of non-essential phrases rather than fundamental disagreements about the answer.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: At least 3 answers per question in development and test sets (1 initial + at least 2 additional).
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Crowdworkers were required to have a 97% HIT acceptance rate, a minimum of 1000 HITs, and be located in the United States or Canada.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Questions with span-based answers are more constrained than more interpretative questions found in advanced standardized tests. Ignoring punctuation and articles, 77.3% of correct answers in the development set are constituents, which places an effective ceiling on the accuracy of methods. Models are challenged more on named entities due to many plausible candidates and perform worst on other answer types (47.6% of the dataset).
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for Reading Comprehension (RC) tasks, training modern data-intensive models, and serving as a challenge problem for future research. It is suitable for Training, Testing, and Validation of machine learning models.
